text:
maria (support): customer reported private agent install failing in their VPC — pip wheels and model shards both 403 or TLS handshake timeout. they say installer hangs at download stage.
maria (support): repro snippet they shared: `curl -Iv https://registry.redwood-internal.example.com/models/abcd` -> TLS handshake timeout; `pip install redwood-agent` -> 403 from files.pythonhosted.org sometimes, then 504s.
kev (eng): thanks. first suspicion: egress proxy / TLS interception or SNI rewrite. do we have a minimal allowlist we can ask them to add?
maria (support): customer wants exact hostnames and ports; they run restricted egress via firewall and explicit allowlist.
jordan (sre): list that usually works for onprem/private installs: `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `registry.redwood.ai` (and internal model shard hostnames), `telemetry.redwood.ai`, `auth.redwood.ai`, `s3.amazonaws.com` (or s3.* region endpoints), `sts.amazonaws.com`, `artifactory.company-cdn.com` if using mirrors. all on 443.
kev (eng): add note: our model shards sometimes come from geo CDN domains and pre-signed S3 URLs. allow outbound 443 to SNI for `*.amazonaws.com` and `*.redwood-internal.example.com` (or the customer-visible registry host). If the org blocks by IP, they need to allow the cloud provider's egress IP ranges — ephemeral ranges cause issues.
maria (support): customer asked about telemetry / auth endpoints for telemetry opt-out during install. can we give exact hosts to allow for auth STS and token exchange?
jordan (sre): auth flows hit `auth.redwood.ai` (443) and `sts.amazonaws.com` for cross-account model pulls. Telemetry goes to `telemetry.redwood.ai` over 443 and uses POSTs. If they want to block telemetry, they can set INSTALL_OPTS to disable telemetry in the installer, but auth still needs to reach token endpoints.
kev (eng): also call out OCSP/CRL and TLS SNI implications — if their proxy MITMs TLS, installer will fail on signature verification for wheels and our model blobs. Recommend allowing passthrough for TLS to the above hostnames (no TLS interception).
maria (support): i'm going to ask them to run these quick checks and paste output: 1) curl with SNI debug 2) openssl s_client 3) traceroute/tcp.
maria (support): suggest commands:```bash
# check SNI & TLS
curl -vI --resolve registry.redwood-internal.example.com:443:52.12.34.56 https://registry.redwood-internal.example.com/models/abcd
# openssl
openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood-internal.example.com:443 -servername registry.redwood-internal.example.com -alpn h2
# pip verbose
PIP_VERBOSE=1 pip --proxy '' install redwood-agent -vv
```
kev (eng): if they see `HTTP/1.1 403` from the CDN fronting S3, ask for the full `curl -v` including response headers; 403 often means the pre-signed URL can't reach S3 or the request is altered (missing Host/SNI).
jordan (sre): infra-bot: please attach the current allowlist KB link so support can forward.
infra-bot: KB / playbook: https://internal.redwood/doc/allowlist-onprem — includes canonical host list and example iptables rules.
maria (support): final ask to customer: please allow outbound TLS (443) to these hostnames (or cloud egress ranges) and re-run the above commands, then paste both `curl -v` and `openssl s_client` output. if they must maintain TLS inspection, have them add exceptions for the registry and pypi hostnames (no interception).
kev (eng): adding troubleshooting tip: if `openssl s_client` returns a certificate issued by their proxy CA (not LetsEncrypt/Amazon), that's the problem. they need to disable interception or provide the proxy CA cert to the agent trust store (not recommended).
maria (support): thanks — i'll relay this and collect their logs. will follow up with an internal replay if they still fail. :thumbsup:
